questions.stem: In a stage's summary metrics, the maximum task duration is 50% or more above the 75th percentile. What does that suggest?

options.text: The cluster has too many nodes
Data skew: one or a few tasks take much longer than the rest

questions.explanation: Skew is when one or a few tasks take much longer than the rest; a max duration 50% or more above the 75th percentile is the sign to look for.

questions.stem: What does spill mean in the Spark UI?

options.text: Data that did not fit in memory was written to disk during the task

questions.explanation: When Spark runs low on execution memory it writes data from memory to disk (spill), which can be expensive.

questions.stem: During which kind of work is spill most common?
questions.explanation: Spill happens when execution memory runs out, and it's most common while data is being shuffled.

questions.stem: A join stage shows heavy skew on one key. Which changes can help? Choose two.

options.text: Switch the job to a file arrival trigger
Make sure adaptive query execution is on so it can split skewed partitions
Spread the hot key with a salt column

questions.explanation: Adaptive query execution can handle skewed joins, and salting spreads a hot key.

questions.stem: Where in the Spark UI do you check whether a stage spilled?

options.text: The stage details at the top of the stage's page

questions.explanation: Spill statistics appear in the stage details at the top of the stage page.
